stories.headline: ECO Council of Ministers convenes in Islamabad for two-day regional meeting
stories.summary: Reporting on 15 November said the 30th Economic Cooperation Organization Council of Ministers meeting was due to begin in Islamabad on Sunday and continue on Monday, with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar chairing. The announcement confirms the schedule, not any negotiated outcome.
stories.background: ECO provides a regional forum for trade, connectivity and economic cooperation among its member states.
stories.what_happened: Pakistan hosted delegations for the scheduled 15–16 November ministerial gathering; as of this partial-day edition, substantive outcomes have not been independently confirmed.
stories.why_it_matters: ECO discussions may affect cross-border trade and transport links, but announced priorities must be distinguished from binding agreements.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan is seeking stronger economic integration and transit connectivity through ECO.
key_takeaways: The 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting was scheduled for 15–16 November 2026 in Islamabad.
Ishaq Dar was announced as chair; decisions were not yet verified.
quick_gk: Islamabad was announced as host of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on 15–16 November 2026.
question_angles: Who was announced as chair of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting in Islamabad?

sources.title: Two-day 30th meeting of ECO to get underway in Islamabad today

stories.headline: Saudi-led coalition reports intercepting Houthi missiles and drones targeting Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 15 November that the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed toward Riyadh and three drones in the Eastern Province. These are coalition-reported interceptions, not independently verified damage assessments.
stories.what_happened: The coalition reported two ballistic missiles and three drones intercepted amid renewed cross-border attacks.
stories.background: Yemen's protracted conflict has repeatedly affected Saudi security and Gulf energy infrastructure.
stories.why_it_matters: Escalation risks for energy facilities and transport can influence global oil markets and regional security.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan is exposed to Gulf energy-market volatility and has important economic and diplomatic ties with Saudi Arabia.
stories.regional_implications: Further strikes could complicate Yemen-related de-escalation and threaten Gulf infrastructure.
key_takeaways: Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two ballistic missiles directed toward Riyadh and three drones in the Eastern Province.
The reported interceptions should not be conflated with confirmed impacts.
quick_gk: On 15 November 2026, the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two Houthi ballistic missiles and three drones.
question_angles: How many ballistic missiles did the Saudi-led coalition report intercepting on 15 November?

sources.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts missiles towards Riyadh, drones in Eastern Province

stories.headline: Fossil-fuel transition coalition plans continued work after Colombia's withdrawal
stories.summary: Associated Press reported on 15 November that a coalition promoting national plans to move away from fossil fuels would continue despite Colombia withdrawing. Ireland and Tuvalu are set to take over leadership, while a progress report is expected at COP31. Proposed plans are not binding climate outcomes.
stories.background: The initiative emerged from a conference in Santa Marta, Colombia, and seeks to translate broad energy-transition commitments into national road maps.
stories.what_happened: The coalition's prospective leadership transition and intended reporting were described; no new binding global treaty was announced.
stories.why_it_matters: The credibility of climate transition pledges depends on concrete implementation, financing and timelines.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Energy-importing developing countries such as Pakistan need feasible financing and grid investment for a transition.
key_takeaways: Ireland and Tuvalu were identified as incoming leaders of the voluntary fossil-fuel transition coalition.
The coalition continues despite Colombia's withdrawal.
quick_gk: Ireland and Tuvalu were identified as incoming leaders of a voluntary fossil-fuel transition coalition in November 2026.
question_angles: Which two countries were identified as incoming leaders of the fossil-fuel transition coalition?

sources.title: Coalition to move away from fossil fuels presses ahead without Colombia, its original champion

stories.headline: Spain reports 1,488 people rescued off Canary Islands in single-day surge
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 15 November that Spain's maritime rescue service rescued 1,488 migrants from 14 boats on Saturday, 14 November, near the Canary Islands. The event occurred on 14 November and is reported here as a 15 November update, not misrepresented as a Sunday rescue.
stories.what_happened: Spanish maritime authorities reported 1,488 people rescued from 14 boats on 14 November.
stories.background: The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands involves dangerous long-distance crossings and places pressure on island reception services.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode raises questions of maritime rescue obligations, migration governance and humanitarian reception capacity.
stories.global_implications: Migration flows and rescue capacity are increasingly important issues for European and African policymakers.
key_takeaways: Spain reported rescuing 1,488 people from 14 boats on 14 November.
The report was published on 15 November; the event date was the preceding day.
quick_gk: Reuters reported on 15 November that Spain rescued 1,488 migrants from 14 boats near the Canary Islands on 14 November 2026.
question_angles: How many boats were involved in the reported 14 November Canary Islands rescue operation?

sources.title: Nearly 1,500 migrants arrive in Canary Islands in one day
